name: ROSETTA
aliases: Refractory Overactive Bladder: Sacral NEuromodulation vs BoTulinum Toxin Assessment
question: Does 200 U intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA reduce urgency urinary incontinence more than staged sacral neuromodulation in women with refractory symptoms?

design.population: 386 randomized women at nine US centers with at least six urgency-incontinence episodes on a three-day diary despite supervised behavioral or physical therapy and at least two anticholinergics or inability to use them.

verdictNote: The six-month episode difference was 0.63 per day; infection and catheterization were more frequent with toxin.
takeaway: In women with refractory urgency urinary incontinence, one 200 U onabotulinumtoxinA injection reduced daily episodes slightly more over six months than staged InterStim sacral neuromodulation (3.9 versus 3.3 fewer; mean difference 0.63), with more urinary tract infections and intermittent catheterization.

reports.label: Six-month randomized comparison
reports.citation: Amundsen CL, Richter HE, Menefee SA, et al. "OnabotulinumtoxinA vs Sacral Neuromodulation on Refractory Urgency Urinary Incontinence in Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2016;316(13):1366-1374. doi:10.1001/jama.2016.14617
reports.followUp: Mean monthly diary change through six months
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA PDF p 3, Outcomes; journal p 1368

results.measure: Mean daily episode reduction averaged over six months; between-group difference in reduction, onabotulinumtoxinA minus SNM
results.note: Prespecified two-sided alpha 0.05; mean difference was smaller than the two-episode difference used for sample-size planning.
results.locator: JAMA PDF p 6, Table 2; journal p 1371

results.measure: Complete urgency-incontinence resolution with at least four monthly diaries through six months; risk difference reported as SNM minus toxin
results.note: Exploratory endpoint; percentage-point risk difference uses the report's SNM-minus-toxin orientation.
results.locator: JAMA PDF p 6, Table 2; journal p 1371

results.measure: Six-month Overactive Bladder Satisfaction of Treatment score; mean difference toxin minus SNM
results.note: Score range 0–100; higher is better. Secondary comparisons were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
results.locator: JAMA PDF p 6, Table 2; journal p 1371

harms.label: Treated urinary tract infection through six months
harms.locator: JAMA PDF p 7, Table 3; journal p 1372
harms.note: UTI included symptomatic or culture-positive treated infection; the report's SNM-minus-toxin risk difference was −23 percentage points (95% CI −33 to −13).

harms.label: Intermittent catheterization after toxin

values.exp: 38/191 (20%) at any visit; 16/191 (8%) at one month; 4/191 (2%) at six months

harms.locator: JAMA PDF p 7, Table 3 and adverse-events text; journal p 1372
harms.note: Median catheterization duration for any reason was 37 days (range 2–203).

harms.label: SNM device revision or removal through six months
harms.locator: JAMA PDF p 7, Table 3; journal p 1372
harms.note: Revision or removal was reported as a combined endpoint.

delivery.label: Operator experience and standardized techniques
delivery.value: Implanters had performed at least 10 InterStim procedures and injectors at least 10 toxin procedures; both reviewed standardized technique videos.

delivery.label: SNM test and implantation
delivery.value: First-stage lead placement under local and monitored anesthesia care, intraoperative sensory and motor testing, then a 7–14-day test; at least 50% diary reduction qualified for permanent generator implantation.

delivery.label: Injection and postvoid residual protocol
delivery.value: Clinic cystoscopic intradetrusor injection of 200 U; intermittent catheterization for residual greater than 300 mL, or greater than 200 mL with incomplete-voiding symptoms.

delivery.label: Treatment received and initial response
delivery.value: 189/192 randomized to toxin received the full injection and 159/192 (83%) responded; 169/189 eligible assigned to SNM had stage-one placement, 142/169 (84%) responded, and 139 received the permanent generator.
delivery.locator: JAMA PDF p 5, Figure 1 and Results; journal p 1370

reports.label: Two-year clinical-responder follow-up
reports.citation: Amundsen CL, Komesu YM, Chermansky C, et al. "Two-Year Outcomes of Sacral Neuromodulation Versus OnabotulinumtoxinA for Refractory Urgency Urinary Incontinence: A Randomized Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2018;74(1):66-73. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2018.02.011
reports.followUp: Twenty-four months among initial clinical responders; outcome data for 260/298 (87%) responders
reports.followUpLocator: PMC6004242 abstract and Results, study population paragraph

results.measure: Mean daily episode reduction across 24 months in initial responders; mean difference in reduction, toxin minus SNM
results.note: Planned extension, but the protocol classified all 24-month analyses as secondary. The abstract gives p=0.15; body text rounds it to p=0.2.
results.locator: PMC6004242 abstract, Results text and Figure 2

results.measure: Mean Overactive Bladder Satisfaction score across 6–24 months; difference SNM minus toxin
results.note: Clinical-responder population; higher score is better.

results.measure: Estimated proportion with no urgency-incontinence episodes at month 24
results.note: Clinical-responder population; Figure 3 estimates, not raw numerator/denominator counts.

harms.label: Recurrent UTI among women without baseline recurrent UTI
harms.note: Recurrent UTI was at least two symptomatic treated infections in six months or three in one year; p<0.01.

harms.label: Any intermittent catheterization over two years after toxin
harms.note: Includes catheterization after any injection during follow-up.

harms.label: SNM revisions and removals over two years
harms.note: Removals: infection 4, decreased efficacy 4, preference 2, pain 2.

delivery.label: Repeat toxin injection
delivery.value: 115/159 (72%) initial toxin responders requested a second injection; median first-to-second interval 350 days. Of those 115, 101 received 200 U and 14 were dose-reduced to 100 U after prolonged catheterization.

delivery.label: SNM reprogramming
delivery.value: 81/139 (58%) implanted initial responders needed reprogramming during 24 months.
